extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: A large-scale, freely and publicly available benchmark dataset for remote sensing image scene classification containing 31,500 images across 45 scene classes with 700 images per class.
extraction.creator: Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Scene classes were selected by reviewing existing datasets and searching literature keywords, and images were extracted by experts from Google Earth covering more than 100 countries and regions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Remote sensing images extracted from Google Earth, which superimposes satellite imagery, aerial photography, and GIS onto a 3D globe.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted and organized into 45 scene classes, with each image sized 256×256 pixels in RGB color space.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Experts in remote sensing image interpretation extracted and assigned images into 45 scene classes.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable the community to develop and evaluate new data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Existing datasets mainly cover limited regions and lack diversity; the proposed dataset addresses this by covering more than 100 countries and regions and including varied economies and imaging conditions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is challenging due to high within-class diversity and between-class similarity, with fine-grained classes that have high semantic overlap.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking, developing, evaluating, and testing scene classification methods and other data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The first step of constructing the dataset is to select a list of representative scene classes. To this end, we first investigated all scene classes of the existing datasets [9, 11, 17, 33, 38, 82] to form 30 widely-used scene categories. Then, we searched the keywords of "OBIA", "GEOBIA", "land cover classification", "land use classification", "geographic image retrieval", and "geospatial object detection" on Web of Science and Google Scholar to carefully select 15 meaningful scene classes. As same as most of the existing datasets [9, 11, 17, 33], this dataset was also extracted, by the experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation, from Google Earth (Google Inc.).

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The creation of this new dataset will enable the community to develop and test various data-driven algorithms to further boost the state-of-the-arts.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Besides, it mainly covers urban areas in China and hence lacks diversity and is less challenging. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: With this in mind, our new dataset is rather challenging with high within class diversity and between class similarity. To this end, we obtained images under all kinds of conditions and added some more fine-grained scene classes with high semantic overlapping such as circular farmland and rectangular farmland, commercial area and industrial area, basketball court and tennis court, and so on.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: This motivates us to propose the NWPU-RESISC45 dataset, which is a freely and publicly available benchmark dataset used for remote sensing image scene classification. The creation of this new dataset will enable the community to develop and test various data-driven algorithms to further boost the state-of-the-arts.
